sn35.138:1.1: “Bhikkhus, whatever is not yours, abandon it.
sn35.138:1.2: When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness.
sn35.138:1.3: And what is it, bhikkhus, that is not yours?
sn35.138:1.4: The eye is not yours: abandon it.
sn35.138:1.5: When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness.
sn35.138:1.8: The mind is not yours: abandon it.
sn35.138:1.9: When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness.
sn35.138:1.10: “Suppose, bhikkhus, people were to carry off the grass, sticks, branches, and foliage in this Jeta’s Grove, or to burn them, or to do with them as they wish. Would you think:
sn35.138:1.11: ‘People are carrying us off, or burning us, or doing with us as they wish’?”
sn35.138:1.14: Because, venerable sir, that is neither our self nor what belongs to our self.”
sn35.138:1.15: “So too, bhikkhus, the eye is not yours …
sn35.138:1.20: When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness.”
